channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Mark Andrews caught both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description: Andrews, somewhat disgustingly, led the team in receiving with a modest 19 yards on a night undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in his first career start. It remains difficult to start the veteran tight end, who has made more mental mistakes this season than he has receptions.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Zay Flowers caught 3-of-6 targets for six yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 17 yards on three carries.
item.description: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did what he could to overcome undrafted free agent rookie Joe Fagnano under center, routinely putting Flowers in Motion across the formation to generate some level of misdirection for an offense with zero ability to attack downfield. That included three rush attempts and a completion thrown by running back Derrick Henry, but it wasn’t enough to salvage a usable fantasy week for the electric receiver. Fantasy managers can rest easy knowing help is on the way in the form of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was signed earlier in the week and will likely make his team debut when the Ravens take on the Chargers in Week 10. Flowers will return to upside WR2 range with the change at quarterback.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Justice Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding seven yards on three receptions.
item.description: Hill became the first running back to amass more than 75 yards against the Jaguars since the start of the 2025 regular season with a 65-yard touchdown with the game well out of hand in the second half. It was an otherwise poor showing for the entirety of the Baltimore offense with a rookie undrafted free agent starting his first NFL game. Hill remains nothing more than desperation FLEX ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Chargers.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Joe Fagnano completed 10-of-18 passes for 60 yards and two interceptions in the Ravens’ 33-10, Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 13 yards on three carries.
item.description: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything he could to scheme around a starting undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first NFL start, calling numerous exotic looks to include direct snaps to Derrick Henry, a Henry pass attempt, quick outs to Zay Flowers, Flowers rush attempts, and flea flickers, but it wasn’t enough to overcome poor execution, consistently off-target throws, and a lack of downfield ability. The Ravens also committed numerous pre-snap penalties as they continue to lead the league in that area through nine weeks, which killed multiple drives. Fagnano managed only 25 pass yards in the first half, finishing with a ridiculous 60 yards, while both interceptions came in the second half with the team in desperation mode. Fagnano leaves his first, and likely last, NFL start with a sour taste in his mouth, as he likely retreats to backup duties following the signing of veteran Jacoby Brissett earlier in the week.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Brenton Strange caught both targets for 22 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description: Strange was overshadowed by the 52-yard reception from fellow tight end Nate Boerkircher on the team’s opening possession, but he made a really nice grab in triple coverage over the middle of the field to set up the team’s second score of the game. Strange remains unlikely to see consistent volume for as long as the Jaguars continue to so handily control games, something that appears likely to continue given the team holds the weakest strength of schedule for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Parker Washington caught 2-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description: Both of Washington’s receptions came before the break, the second of which was a 50-yard touchdown on a double-move slant against Cover-0 with under one minute remaining before the half. Washington remains one of the most efficient receivers in the league but consistently positive game scripts have left the overall pass volume lacking, particularly in the second half this season. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description: All four of Meyers’ receptions came before the half in what remained a tighter game until just before the half, when alpha wide receiver Parker Washington took a simple slant for a 50-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining before the break. As has been the case on numerous occasions this season, Jacksonville coasted in the second half, limiting overall pass volume after the break. Meyers narrowly missed his first touchdown since Week 3 as he was tackled at the one on the team’s first possession. He remains a viable FLEX option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
item.description: Rodriguez split time with lead back Bayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description: Tuten started after failing to practice in any capacity this week, capping off the opening drive with a score from one yard out. He would split time with Chris Rodriguez for the rest of the first half before giving way to the combination of Rodriguez and special teams ace Ameer Abdullah for the bulk of the second half with the game in hand. Tuten should see his volume tick back up toward lead back territory when the Jaguars face off against the Titans in Week 10, where he will return to RB2 status.-Mark Garcia
